result.summary:
I checked the domestic research against re-fetched sources and redid the NAIP measurements. Two cited facts are wrong, one roof section was misread, and every NAIP height should come down about 5 %. The Verification section is appended to the research note and the corrections are in the spec. I changed nothing in js/ or data/ and committed nothing. (spec_itb.json and itb_verify.* in the working tree come from another agent, not from me.)

**Refuted**
- **"T1 skylight trusses 70 ft above the floor, four 180 × 30 ft reflectors"**: the SFO Museum page puts this artwork in the Dianne Feinstein International Terminal main hall (Level 3, dated 2000). "Harvey Milk Terminal 1" only appears in the page's menu of terminals. T1 Center therefore has no published height at all. The skylight-count "conflict" goes away: Airport Improvement 2020 says three skylights, which matches the three openings seen on NAIP. These figures belong to the ITB research.
- **BA-D DOF points "at the head corners" (24–25 ft)**: all three lie 24–37 m outside the BA-D outline, and the DOF horizontal accuracy is ±6 m, so they are not on the pier and cannot check its height. DOF 06-035332 (16 ft) is also on the apron, 9 m past the BA-F tip, not part of BA-F.
- **The research's own tower note** (axis 7 m east of the tower research) is not a real conflict. It came from the 2020 shadow scale below; with the corrected scale the axis lands at about −737 to −741.

**Corrected**
- **2020 shadow scale (sets every NAIP height)**: the research used 1.19 m of shadow per metre "± 0.03". At its own tower-shadow direction (87.4°) the sun path gives 1.226. I re-measured the direction at 88.1–88.9°, which gives 1.26–1.31. The BA-F DOF control fits about 1.27 best; only the BA-A lean check supports 1.19. I adopted 1.25 (range 1.19–1.31), so the heights below are about 5 % lower than in the research:

| Roof | Research | Adopted | Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| BA-A (control) | 18.74 m | 17.83 m | 16.94–18.74 m (ITB research: 17.0) |
| BA-E fascia | 13.51 m | 12.85 m | 12.21–13.51 m |
| BA-F north-east arm | 11.03 m | 10.49 m | 9.97–11.03 m (DOF: 10.36 m) |
| BA-D head (low confidence) | 8.92 m | 8.49 m | 8.07–8.93 m |
| BA-C (low confidence) | 7.54 m | 7.20 m | 6.99–7.53 m |

- **Boarding Area B is stepped, not one level**: measured on the south half only, the central PV field moves 3.40 m between 2020 and 2024, but the side bands and outer edges move only 2.25–2.30 m, so they are lower. The 2020 "dark perimeter strip" is the shadow of the raised central roof on the lower band; it is white roof in 2024. The research had combined the central roof's parallax with the outer edge's shadow bands.
  - Outer edges: 13.1 m (12.5–13.8). The research's 12.87 m was close only because two errors cancelled.
  - New raised central roof: 19.0 m (18.1–20.0). The roughly 6 m step is the clerestory Arup describes.
  - Recomputed edge overhang: about 2.3 m on the airfield side (was 3.3 m).
- **Smaller fixes**: PV row width 5.7–7.1 m (the 9.1–9.3 m pitch is confirmed). The T3W "22'-0"" is the sum of printed 10'+10'+2' dimensions, not a printed value. The author of photos p17–p20 is Benoît Prieur (the spec had HTML junk).

**Confirmed**
- **T3 levels** from the re-fetched design-review PDF: L1 11'-0", L2 27'-0", mezzanine 42'-6", L3 45'-0", roof high points R2 58'-6" and R3 81'-0", T3W parapet 66'-0".
- **Wall sections**: field 56'-00" with a 42" parapet, gatehouse 59'-07".
- **SFO Museum outlines**: confirmed as level-2 floor outlines.
- **The BA-E roof** is one level; its parallax is uniform at about 2.6 m.
- **Dates, areas, gate counts, PV and glazing figures** were all re-read in the original sources.
- **All 26 photo licences** match Commons.
- **The two-epoch method's algebra** holds, as long as every measurement belongs to the same roof edge.

**Still unknown**
- **T1 Center and T2 hall heights.** Nothing is published.
- **The datum of the T3 elevations.**
- **The exact 2020 sun.** The acquisition time of the 2020 image strips would pin every NAIP height to about ±2 %. I tried to read pole shadows of known height on NAIP 2020 instead, but none could be picked out at 0.6 m resolution.
- **BA-B north half and roof wells.** The parallax scan was not done there.
- **Truss rhythm and facade bays.** No source gives them.

The checks re-run with `python3 tools/buildings/dom_verify.py`, and `--apply` rewrites the spec records. NAIP 2020 and 2022 can still be fetched from Planetary Computer with `dom_naip_epochs.py`, so the missing second epoch is not a blocker.
open_questions: NAIP 2020 acquisition time per strip over SFO (USDA APFO seamline / flight-log metadata) to fix |s20| (adopted 1.25, range 1.19-1.31)
BA-B section: an SFO/HKS section drawing or a scaled photo of the clerestory step; parallax scan of the north half and roof wells
T3 CDR elevation datum vs NAVD88 / apron (SFO Design & Construction)
T1 Center and T2 main-hall roof heights: nothing published
ITB research should take the SFO Museum figures (main-hall skylight trusses 70 ft above Level 3, four 180 x 30 ft reflectors, 2000)

result.summary:
I fact-checked the ITB research and appended a '## Verification' section to docs/research/buildings_itb.md. It holds 34 claims, each with a verdict and its evidence, plus sections V.2–V.4. Two values in tools/buildings/spec_itb.json were wrong and are corrected, with the old values kept. One measured width was refuted (Boarding Area G's ~33.5 m) and two numbers were relabelled. The 860 ft roof-length conflict is still open. Nothing was committed, and js/ and data/ are untouched.

How it was checked: tools/buildings/itb_verify.py repeats everything offline in about 5 s and writes tools/buildings/itb_verify.json (numbers only). Run with --apply, it writes the verdicts into the spec; all 65 items now carry a verification record. Because build_spec_itb.py regenerates the spec without them, run itb_verify.py --apply again after it.
- Re-fetched: the FAA DOF (file dated 2026-11-02), 15 source pages and the Commons licence records of all 24 photos. Each download's URL and licence is recorded in a SOURCES.json beside it.
- itb_naip_measure.py on the restored NAIP 2024 raster gives byte-identical output.
- The SEAONC page, previously read only as search snippets, now opens and was read in full.

**Verified**
- **DOF roof tops:** 06-035315 and 06-035316 are unchanged at 131 / 132 ft AGL, accuracy 1A. They were added to the DOF on 16 Oct 2013, so the survey predates NAIP 2024 and the re-roofing.
- **Column lines:** the two DOF points sit at u = +57.2 / −58.4 m from the relief-corrected centre. They are 115.5 m (379 ft) apart along the axis, which matches the 380 ft centre span. They mark the roof over the inner column lines (±190 ft), which independently supports the inferred column rhythm. The note's "+54.7 / −60.9 m" was measured from the uncorrected (as-imaged) centre; that is now corrected.
- **Now read first-hand (SEAONC):** five double-cantilever truss sets; 20 cantilevered columns rising from the level-3 departures floor; trusses up to 29 ft deep; 380 ft centre span; 160 ft end cantilevers; 860 ft overall; great hall 705 × 210 × up to 83 ft (so 83 ft is the interior height, not the roof height); Herrick, Mare Island, about 35 pieces by barge.
- **Axis:** 162.81°, from an independent fit to the west facade base (sd 0.15 m). That is the airport grid t-axis + 135°, and both piers also sit on the grid axes.
- **Width:** 65.4 m. The east eave rises and falls along the roof together with the west eave, so the measured "wing" profile is a height signal, not a curved plan.
- **Truss spacing:** 12.16 m = 39.9 ft, by autocorrelation over 207 rows (published 40 ft).
- **Sun:** solar-position formulas give 13:14 PDT and 72.39° elevation for the NAIP flight date.
- **Glazed tip bands:** confirmed visually.
- **Published figures:** levels, dates (10 Dec 2000 opening, 16 Jan 2024 renaming, 27 Jun 2024 ceremony, mid-2026 completion), 1.8 M sq ft, 267 isolators, the Boarding Area G facts (Tutor Perini) and 1,400 kW of PV were each found verbatim in the cached pages.
- **Photos:** all 24 licences and authors match the spec.

**Corrected**
- **Roof corners:** the stated outline is 255.06 m long, which contradicts the spec's own length of 252.68 m. It is replaced by corners from a frame-camera relief model fitted to the same five pole picks (252.87 × 65.39 m). The old corners are kept as an alternative.
- **Boarding Area A roof:** 17.0 → 17.9 m (range 16.9–18.8). The west band re-measures 8.79 m. The note subtracted a roof overhang, but an overhang moves both band edges equally and cancels out; its second method depended on the SFO Museum footprint.
- **Refuted:** Boarding Area G's measured roof width is 38.4 m between its parapets, not ~33.5 m. That matches the SFO Museum body width.
- **Weaker than stated:** the A pod rim band includes the pod's own shadow, so the pod rises 4.9–5.2 m above the main roof, not 7.5 m. That gives a pod top of 22.3–25.2 m against the DOF's 25.9 m.
- **Minor:** the 48.4 m lens skylight length is the as-imaged length; true is about 47.9 m.
- **Conflict:** gates at opening are 26 per SEAONC and 24 per Tutor Perini.

**New uncertainty and findings**
- **Relief model:** fitting the five pole shifts in both directions with a frame camera works better than the east-only model (rms 0.21 vs 0.54 m), and the shift direction turns with north–south position. But two of the five picks are by eye, and Boarding Area G's visible shadow contradicts a single frame there. The NAIP 2024 sensor is undocumented in any open source I found.
  - Roof length is therefore 252.6–255.1 m, still 7–9 m short of the published 860 ft (262.1 m).
  - With the inner columns fixed by the DOF pair, the visible cantilever beyond the outer column is about 145 ft, not 160 ft.
- **Centre section off-centre:** it sits 2.2 m north of the midpoint between the fascias. The south tip has a 3.6 m white strip beyond its glass; the north tip has 1.6 m.

**Still unknown:** the roof length conflict; the 320 ft truss length and 180 ft centre section (the AISC article is still blocked); the crown and tip heights, which rest on a photo I could not re-measure because Wikimedia returned HTTP 429; the level-3 floor (only bracketed at 9.6–14.8 m); pier pod heights; the 2026 roof's PV layout; the $75 M cost; and whether the skylights are lens- or D-shaped in plan.
open_questions: Roof length: NAIP 252.6-255.1 m vs 860 ft (262.1 m) published. The DOF pair confirms the 380 ft centre span, so the gap is in the end cantilevers (about 145 ft visible vs 160 ft published). An SFO record roof plan, a tip survey or the NAIP 2024 frame metadata would settle it.

NAIP 2024 sensor and mosaic seamlines: the north-south relief component is unresolved. The poles favour a frame camera (nadir about (-2768, 444)), but Boarding Area G contradicts a single frame. This sets the length range and the pier heights.
AISC Modern Steel Construction Feb 2000 is still unreadable (curl 403, WebFetch 403, web.archive.org connection reset), so the 320 ft truss length and 180 ft centre section remain snippet-only.
The crown and tip heights rest on the DimiCalifornia photo, which could not be re-fetched (Wikimedia HTTP 429). Re-run itb_photo_skyline.py once the rate limit clears.
Pier heights: A main roof 17.4-18.3 m, pods 22.3-25.2 m by relief against the DOF's 25.9 m; G 16.9 m (east-only relief model). No published elevations.
The 'SFO Museum G outline is 3-6 m NNE of the NAIP roof' claim was not re-checked.
The RADP NOP (main-hall and A/G expansions) was not re-fetched this round.

result.summary:
I fact-checked the landside building research and appended a `## Verification` section to `docs/research/buildings_landside.md` (section 14, same layout as the tower's). Every one of the 130 values in `spec_landside.json` now carries a verdict:
- 84 confirmed, 18 of them with a qualifier;
- 2 plausible;
- 4 disputed, 6 corrected and 1 refuted;
- 1 still unknown;
- 28 not re-checked;
- 4 new.

Corrected values keep their old fields and the reason under `corrected`.

**How I checked**
- 43 sources re-fetched and re-read.
- FAA DOF checked against the newer DOF.CSV of 2026-11-03.
- SFO Museum building records re-read.
- NAIP 2024 re-measured with methods different from the original:
  - a 2-D roof-shift scan;
  - the helix-drum facade bands, using the ITB pole calibration inside its valid range;
  - north shadows on flat ground, against the solar position for 20 May 2024.

**Refuted or corrected**
- **RCC "NAIP 19.5 m agrees with 66 ft":** refuted. The original used the third-strongest roof-shift peak and a lean model that doesn't hold in the North Field. The DOF survey puts the roof outline at 54 ft (three points) and 59 ft (one), all on the west side, not the NE corner. It also lists a 34-ft obstacle the research missed. The published 66 ft is confirmed as text but can't be the parapet height.
- **Central garage built 1981, replacing an earlier 1963–1981 garage:** corrected. The RADP historic resources study says Building 195 was built in phases from 1963 to 1981. The 1963–65 first section was partly demolished and absorbed, and the garage was completed in 1980–81.
- **Superbay layout:**
  - The cantilever is "over 230 ft from the center", so the "2 × 70 m + spine" breakdown is wrong.
  - NAIP shows a roof 165 m long with a 32 m spine (not 25–30 m).
  - Each side is folded into 8 bays of 17.3 m. This conflicts with Deep3DS's "50 foot wide structural bays", which the research missed.
- **One NAIP moment at about 13:25 for every building:** corrected. The Superbay area was imaged in the morning, so the roof-car counts aren't one moment.
- **One lean factor across the landside area:** refuted outside its calibrated range. The lean factor is about 0.30–0.33 m per m of height at the CAC and Long-Term Parking (LTP) Garage 1. The model gives 0.14–0.19 there.
- **LTP Garage 2 "four seismically isolated structures":** corrected to "seismically separated". The count of four rests only on the Buehler page, which no longer loads.

**Disputed**
- **Garages A and G at 25–30 m:** NAIP puts the helix-drum tops at 39.6 m (A) and 37.6 m (G), about ±2 m. The parking roof deck itself is still unmeasured.
- **Build years:** the RADP appendix gives 1994 for LTP Garage 1 and 1998 for the RCC; the SFO Museum records give approximate years of 1997 and 2000.

**Confirmed**
- Central garage: 81 ft, five levels, 3.68 M sq ft, 6,460 spaces, 200-ft void (measured hole 58.7–59.0 m).
- Garages A and G: nine levels, AirTrain at Level 7.
- LTP Garage 2: 6 levels, 12-ft floors, 3,600 stalls, completed 2020.
- RCC: 5 levels, 1,488,000 sq ft, 2,485 stalls, Building 780.
- Grand Hyatt: 12 stories, 4th-floor lobby, Building 55, opened 7 Oct 2019.
- CAC: 4 stories at 15 ft, 135,000 sq ft (the 136,000 figure is gone), Phase II addendum. It is Building 674.
- CAC height of about 64 ft: within ±1.5 m. The north shadow gives 17.4–19.2 m; the old 28.6 m scan value is refuted.
- Superbay: four bays, six office levels, 120 ft inside, DOF 135 ft. That DOF entry is a 2011 change, not part of the 2013 survey batch.
- LTP Garage 1: the DOF points of 86 and 91 ft are confirmed. A new shadow measurement puts the north-end parapet at 15.9–16.8 m, so those points are elements about 10 m higher.
- AirTrain: car size 9'3" × 39'6", $430 M, 1,900-ft extension, the "50 ft" and "35–40 ft" quotes, opening 24 Feb / official 3 Mar 2003.
- All nine footprints, the 2018 parking supply, and the A/G station-name swap in the SFO Museum data.

**Still unknown**
- Grand Hyatt height (provisional 44 m). Its SFO Museum outline doesn't trace the main slab.
- Garage A/G and LTP Garage 2 roof decks.
- What the 81 ft and 66 ft actually measure.
- The 13 photo licences: the Commons API returned HTTP 429, so I couldn't re-check them.

**Tooling**
- `tools/buildings/landside_verify.py` runs offline in about 15 s. `tools/buildings/landside_verify_apply.py` writes the corrections into the spec.
- `build_spec_landside.py` now calls the apply step. I checked that a rebuild plus apply gives an identical spec and that re-running changes nothing.
- `landside_fetch.py` now falls back to `pdftotext` when PyMuPDF is missing.
- I added `SOURCES.json` files beside the cached downloads.

Nothing in `js/` or `data/` was touched, and nothing was committed.
open_questions: Garages A/G: the roof-deck height (the drum tops measure 37.6–39.6 m). Needs an SFO drawing, the station platform elevation at Level 7, or a north shadow on flat ground.
What the published 81 ft (Central garage) and 66 ft (RCC) measure. The DOF puts the RCC roof outline at 54–59 ft.
Grand Hyatt height: needs an SFO GIS ground outline of the slab or the FAA obstruction filing; the provisional 44 m is still an inference.
Superbay: are the 17.3-m roof folds the structural bays, or is Deep3DS's 50 ft right? Needs a drawing or a photo with a scale.
Build years: RADP appendix 1994 / 1998 against SFO Museum ~1997 / ~2000 for LTP Garage 1 and the RCC.
Re-check the 13 Commons photo licences when the API is no longer rate-limited (HTTP 429 on 2026-11-04).
NAIP 2024 frame metadata (nadir per frame) would turn every measured east shift into a height; the single lean model is invalid outside the ITB range.

result.summary:
I drew the building sheets and published nothing outside the allowed paths. js/, data/ and docs/research/ are untouched, and nothing was committed. Your WIP snapshots already contain early versions of draw_lib.py, draw_data.py, draw_measure.py and deviations.json; the files on disk are newer.

There are 12 vector sheets (SVG + PNG, no imagery pixels, 5.5 MB in total) and 4 NAIP 2024 overlays (local only). All are drawn from the four verified spec JSONs. `python3 tools/buildings/draw.py` rebuilds everything in about 45 s and does not use Chromium. Each sheet has a title block, scale bars, a north arrow on plans, dimension lines and level marks. Every value carries a [tag source] label, and the line style also shows the tag: pub black solid, obs blue solid, inf orange dashed italic, unknown grey dotted, app magenta.

**Sheets (docs/drawings/buildings/)**
- **Tower** (BT-01 plan 1:400; BT-02 ESE and WNW elevations 1:200; BT-03 section 1:400). The tower verification asked for both height families to be drawn: the spec values (rim 67.36 m, D 14.3) are solid and family 2 (rim 64.0 m, D 14.5, 221 ft at the mast tips) is dotted. BT-01 also shows the cab x bounds, the OE/AAA sites, the cab as imaged in four NAIP epochs, and the app's shaft and cab.
- **ITB** (BI-01 roof plans: key 1:2500, hall 1:750, BA-A / BA-G; BI-02 west and north elevations; BI-03 long and cross sections). The hall roof is relief-corrected: 252.9 × 65.4 m, 5 truss lines at 12.12 m, 5 lens skylights, glazed tip bands, the DOF tops at 40.08 m and the eave profile. Column lines and truss taper are marked inferred. The 860 ft published length is drawn next to the measured length as a conflict.
- **Domestic** (BD-01 plan 1:2500; BD-02 pier cross-sections 1:500 and the T3 West CDR wall sections and level datum 1:200). The plan shows the SFO Museum level-2 outlines, the measured lean-free roof edges, the pier heights with ranges, and the refuted DOF points.
- **Landside** (BL-01 key plan 1:5000; BL-02 roof plans 1:2000; BL-03 long-face elevations 1:1000). All buildings and DOF points, including the Superbay spine and roof bays and the United MOC from its imaged roof.
- **BX-01, app vs spec** (A2): a 28-row table, a heights dot plot, and tower and ITB profile overlays. The biggest gaps:
  - The ITB roof is built to the 83-ft interior height (21–26.5 m against 34.9–40.1 m) and sits 35 m east of the measured roof, turned 2.9°.
  - The tower shaft is 7.2 m south of the inferred axis; the cab roof is D 20.3 against 14.3–14.75, and the rim is 1–5.5 m too low.
  - Every pier is 14.6 m against measured 7.2–19.0 m.
  - The Superbay, RCC and Hyatt heights are off, and the MOC is not built.

**Deviations method.** NAIP roofs are displaced by relief, so a drawn roof edge is compared at its predicted imaged position (height × lean). Footprints are checked only on faces towards the camera nadir, where the facade base is visible. The lean model is per area: a frame model fitted to the FAA DOF poles for the ITB and tower, per-pier two-epoch leans for the domestic piers, the measured North Field lean, and a fitted (circular) lean at the Superbay. Each edge's offset is in deviations.json, and the README explains how to read the results.

**Results.**
- SFO Museum outlines match the visible facade bases within about 1 m (the Superbay is 2.8 m off).
- The domestic level-2 outlines are 1–3 m off the roofs, as the spec says.
- The ITB roof is consistent to 0.3 m, but that check uses the same imagery the roof was measured on.
- The frame model predicts the NAIP cab disc within (1.1, 1.1) m for a 67.36 m rim and (2.9, 1.0) m for 64.0 m. That leans towards a 221-ft rim but does not settle it, because the cab x is itself ±5 m.

**README.md** has the sheet list, what is verified / inferred / unknown for each group, the overlay method, a results table and the limits.
open_questions: Tower height family: the spec set (rim 67.36 m, D 14.3) is about 3 m inconsistent. The 3-D tower should not be built from one value until a surveyed photo, the NAIP shadow with the flight time, or an SFO/FAA elevation drawing decides between rim at 221 ft and 221 ft at the mast tips. The NAIP cab-disc check only weakly favours the 221-ft rim.
ITB roof length: the published 860 ft (262.1 m) against 252.6-255.1 m measured on NAIP is still open, and both are drawn. Which should the 3-D use?
Terminal 3 West state to model: under construction 2024-2029, with a May 2026 design change adding one airside storey. The owner's choice.

Unpublished heights are drawn as ranges or placeholders: T1 Center and T2 halls (nothing), Garages A/G roof decks (only the helix drum tops), Grand Hyatt (~44 m inferred), and United MOC section heights.
The vector PNGs add 5.5 MB to docs/drawings/buildings, which is not covered by the docs/drawings/*.png gitignore. Commit the PNGs and SVGs, or SVG only?

findings.where: README 'Control tower ... Overlay check' and the BT-01_naip.jpg leader text ('leans towards the 221-ft rim')
findings.problem: The cab-disc check cannot tell the two height families apart, but the README reads it as evidence for the 221-ft rim. The two families' predicted imaged centres differ by 1.9 m in x. Two uncertainties in the inputs are each larger than that: the cab x itself, and the frame model's flying height.
findings.evidence: deviations.json tower_cab_check: delta [1.06, 1.1] (67.36 m) vs [2.94, 0.98] (64.0 m), a 1.88 m difference. Inputs: cab x = -739 +- 5 [inf], from OSM/Google traced on lean-affected imagery (spec verification: 'not independent'). Frame model: H_minus_h_sd 277.3 m (spec naip.k_model.alt_frame_model). At the cab that is about +-3 m on the 37 m lean. The k(x) model gives the same two predictions (-701.8 / -703.7), so a second model does not help.
findings.fix: State that the check is inconclusive (difference smaller than the input uncertainty). Remove 'leans towards'.

findings.where: docs/drawings/buildings/README.md 'Control tower ... Verified' and 'ITB ... Verified'
findings.problem: The README's 'Verified' lists include values that the spec verification did not verify.
findings.evidence: Listed under 'Verified': 'flare 22.6 m; waist 9.8 m; 10.3 m at the base-building roof' and 'cab roof 14.3 +- 1.0'. In spec_tower.json, d_shaft_waist, d_shaft_at_ibf_roof, d_cab_glass_top and d_cab_glass_bottom have no verification block at all. d_cab_roof is 'PLAUSIBLE (within tolerance); stated derivation flawed' and d_flare_max is 'PLAUSIBLE'. For the ITB, 'Verified' includes the 40.1 m crown, but the roof.profile verification says "The photo silhouette was not re-run (Commons API rate-limited, file not cached)".

findings.where: BI-01 view 2 (hall roof plan), BI-02 (tip bands), tools/buildings/draw_itb.py draw_hall_roof / lens_poly
findings.problem: Three parts of the hall roof plan contradict the measurement record and its verification. (a) The glazed tip bands are drawn starting at the fascia, but the measured glass ends 1.6 m (N) and 3.6 m (S) inside the fascia. (b) The lens row is drawn centred on the fascia midpoint, but it was measured ~1-2.2 m north of it. (c) The westmost lens is drawn 33.7 m long and labelled 'the westmost 34 m', although the verification found it is full length.
findings.evidence: itb_naip_measurements.json roof_length.tips: N_outer -125.0 vs fascia N -126.625, and S_outer 125.0 vs fascia S 128.625. spec roof.glazed_tips_obs verification: 'beyond the glass the south tip carries a 3.6 m white segmented strip, the north tip 1.6 m' and 'the centre-section lens row sits 2.2 m north' of the fascia midpoint. Lens boxes u0/u1 are about +-24.25 around imaged u 0 (centroids u_c -0.5..-1.25); the fascia midpoint is at imaged +1.0. draw_itb draws the bands at (-HL, -HL+18.75) and (HL-15.75, HL) and places the lenses at uc*MAG about the fascia midpoint F['c']. spec roof.lenses_obs verification: 'The westmost lens is full length too (detected 34 m because it is darker)'. lens_poly(0) gives a length of 33.66 m.
findings.fix: Offset the bands by 1.6 / 3.6 m and shift the lens row about 2 m north. Draw lens 0 at full length.

findings.where: BI-01_naip.jpg view 4 and the deviations.json / README rows for Boarding Area G (lean 'frame')
findings.problem: The BA-G overlay deviations use the single-frame relief model, which the spec says fails at BA-G. The reported BA-G roof numbers depend on that choice.
findings.evidence: spec_itb ba_g.height_roof verification: "Under the single-frame relief model the roof would hide its own shadow -> G is in another frame of the mosaic or has little north-south relief"; that height was re-measured with k(x). At G the frame model gives a lean of (0.357, -0.094) m/m, i.e. 1.6 m of N-S relief at 17 m. Re-running draw_measure.measure_ring on BA-G with k(x) east-only changes the roof result from median -0.60 / |med| 1.46 / 72 % <= 2.5 m (reported) to +0.13 / 1.05 / 88 %. The base result is unchanged (-0.57 vs -0.64).
findings.fix: Use k(x) at BA-G (as the spec does), or report both models.

findings.where: BI-02 view 1 (west elevation), tools/buildings/draw_itb.py west_elev / crown()
findings.problem: Two drawing errors in the ITB profile. The '+40.1 centre crown' level mark is drawn 1.6 m above its own value. The drawn roof profile also has a 0.55 m step at |u| = 27 m, where the photo crown curve hands over to the NAIP eave curve.
findings.evidence: `V.level(-HL - 2, CROWN + 1.6, f'+{CROWN} centre crown ...', u_line=0)` draws the line at 41.7 m, above the '+40.08 humps' mark. In BI-02.png it sits ~8 px above the 40.08 line and does not touch the dashed crown peak. Computed: crown(26.9) = 35.70 m, eave(27) = crown(27) = 36.25 m. The spec full_curve never reaches the 35.7 'notch' (minimum 35.79 at |u| 23).
findings.fix: Draw the level at 40.1 and move only the label. Blend crown() into eave() at |u| 27.

findings.where: BI-02 table 'Heights and their sources', row 'Roof "60 to 90 ft above the floor"'
findings.problem: The level-3 range is attributed to the wrong source and tagged pub.
findings.evidence: The row reads '-> L3 9.6-12.7 m [pub] Smith-Emery / MSC'. Per spec level3.floor, 12.7 m = 40.1 m minus '90 ft' (Smith-Emery), but 9.6 m = 40.1 m minus '100 ft' (sfgate2000). The '60 to 90 ft' figure alone gives 12.7-21.8 m. The derived L3 is inf, not pub.
findings.fix: Use 'L3 = DOF top - 90 ft (Smith-Emery) / - 100 ft (sfgate2000) = 12.7 / 9.6 m [inf]'.

findings.where: BI-01 view 3 (Boarding Area A) labels
findings.problem: The BA-A pod labels conflict with each other and the conflict is not flagged. A pod-1 lengths value that the verification revised is shown unchanged.
findings.evidence: Labels: 'main roof 17.9 m', 'pod 1 +4.9-5.2 m above the main roof [obs]' and 'pod 1: 25.9 m (DOF) [pub]'. 17.9 + 5.2 = 23.1 m, which is 2.8 m short of the DOF. The spec verification says 'pod top 22.3-25.2 m ... consistent only at its upper end'. 'pods 70 / 55 / 55 m [obs, by eye]' is drawn, but the verification says 'Pod 1 reads ~55-60 m long by eye (note: 70)'.

findings.where: BD-02 view 2, Terminal 3 West field wall (tools/buildings/draw_domestic.py sheet_elev)
findings.problem: The field-wall windows are placed above L2 with the note 'vertical position not dimensioned - placed at L2 [inf]'. The spec verification reads the printed 10'-0" + 2'-0" + 10'-0" chain as the 22'-0" between the international level and the top of the parapet, so the window stack is dimensioned and belongs above L3.
findings.evidence: spec_domestic t3w.wall_field verification: "the field section prints 10'-00", 18'-00", 16'-00", 56'-00", 10'-00", 2'-00" and 0'-42" ...: the 22'-0" above the international level is the sum 10 + 10 + 2 ft". The drawing places windows at 18-28 ft and 30-40 ft above L1, across the +10.36 m (34 ft) international line.

findings.where: BL-03 (landside elevations) and its note 2; tools/buildings/draw_landside.py sheet_elev
findings.problem: BL-03 states things that are not in the spec. (a) The 25 m lower bound of the Garage A/G roof-deck band is explained as '9 levels at ~2.8 m [inf]'. In the spec that bound is what remains of the disputed '25-30 m' photo reading. (b) The RCC 'station tower 60 ft [pub DOF]' is a DOF TANK whose identity is [inf]. (c) DOF masts on the central garage (u 120/180/230 m) and LTP 1 (u 30/140 m) are drawn at arbitrary positions in pub style.
findings.evidence: spec_landside garage_a_height.corrected.old.range_m [25, 36] (from the photo); verdict 'DISPUTED (the 25-30 m photo reading)'. No '2.8 m' derivation exists in the spec or in buildings_landside.md. rcc_dof: 'TANK 60 ft (06-034240) ... 6.4 m west of the outline' and 'The "TANK" matches the cylindrical ... stair/elevator tower ... [inf]'. The DOF re-fetch (DOF.CSV 2026-11-03) gives 06-034240 TYPE TANK.
findings.fix: Cite the real basis or drop the lower bound. Tag the tower identity inf. Place the masts at the projected DOF positions, or mark their positions as schematic.

findings.where: BX-01 table and README 'The app today vs the spec'
findings.problem: The BX-01 table misdescribes the app's ITB columns and understates the app's roof height.
findings.evidence: js/live/terminals.js greatHall: `for (const sg of [-1, 1]) for (let j = 0; j < 10; j++) { const t = -hallW/2 + 2 + (hallW-4)*j/9; const s = sg * colS; ...}`. That is 2 transverse rows of 10 at the inner column lines (s = +-57.9 m) across the width. BX-01 says '2 x 10 along the long edges'. The app roof is `crown(s,t) = top(s) + 0.6*(1-(t/(W/2))^2)`, so the app maximum is 27.1 m, not 26.5 m.
findings.fix: Correct the row text, and use the crown in the app range.

findings.where: docs/drawings/buildings/README.md results table, row 'Lean-free roof-edge lines B / D / F | line | <= 0.2'
findings.problem: The README reports all six lean-free roof-edge lines as checked to within 0.2 m. One of them, the BA-F WNW line, was not measured.
findings.evidence: deviations.json summary: 'Boarding Area F (lean-free roof edge, WNW) line 0/1 ok, median None' (weak edge).
findings.fix: State '5 of 6 lines; F WNW weak'.

findings.where: BT-02 / BT-03 (tower silhouette vs dimensions)
findings.problem: The drawn flare silhouette and the flare dimension disagree. The plan shows the cab offset from the shaft but the elevations draw it concentric.

The verification also notes the A380 ratios are ~1.5 % high. BT-01 draws the cab at (-739, 323.5) and the axis at (-740.5, 324.5): u offset +1.6 m in view A, -1.6 m in view B. findings.where: tools/buildings/draw_lib.py View.background / naip_rgb (all *_naip.jpg overlays)
findings.problem: In the overlays, the NAIP background image is slightly misplaced. The crop is snapped outward to whole pixels and then stretched to the exact view limits, so content near the view edges is off by up to 0.4 m. The measured deviations are not affected.
findings.evidence: naip_rgb crops columns floor((x0-X0)/R) .. ceil((x1-X0)/R), but imshow uses extent=[x0, x1]. Computed misplacement at the view edges: BT-01 0.4 m (x) / 0.1 m (z); BI-01 views 1-2 0.25 m; BD-01 and BL-02 0. sample_lum (used by measure_edge) applies the pixel-centre convention correctly.
findings.fix: Pass the snapped crop bounds as the imshow extent.

findings.where: BT-01 (OE/AAA site 13 = DOF 06-323169 mark) vs the BI/BD/BL sheets' DOF marks
findings.problem: The tower's DOF point uses a different datum conversion from every other sheet. It is plotted with the NAD83 conversion, while the ITB, domestic and landside code convert DOF coordinates as WGS 84 (per DOF_README), so it sits 1.6 m west of where the other sheets' convention would put it. A sample re-fetch of the sources otherwise confirms the sheets' DOF and SEAONC values.
findings.evidence: geo_frame: ll_to_world(37.61578056, -122.38382778) = (-742.6, 335.7) (drawn), wgs84_to_world = (-741.0, 335.9). itb_naip_measure.py:63, landside_common.py:93 and dom_common.py:77 use wgs84_to_world. Re-fetched DAILY_DOF_CSV (DOF.CSV 2026-11-03) for 24 points: 06-035315/316 131/132 ft 1A, 06-035352 85, 06-035331/332 34/16, 06-035330/321/320 25/24/25, 06-035351 50, 06-323169 245 ft R 4D, MOC 116/132/117, RCC 54/59/54/54 + TANK 60 + 34, LTP1 91/86, CG 109/101/130 (4D), Superbay 06-001451 135 ft R 1A. All heights, lighting and accuracies match the sheets, and positions match to 0.1 m under wgs84_to_world. SEAONC re-fetched: 29 ft / 380 / 160 / 860 ft, 20 columns from level 3, 705 x 210 x 83 ft confirmed verbatim.
findings.fix: Use one datum convention for all DOF marks, or label the tower point as the OE/AAA NAD83 position.

findings.where: docs/drawings/buildings/BT-02 view B (WNW, landside) and BT-01 plan; tools/buildings/draw_tower.py draw_tower_elev(ribbon=True)
findings.problem: The landside of the tower is drawn as a round body of revolution with the glass ribbon pasted on as a flat dark trapezoid. Only grey dotted 'unk' fin lines are drawn, and only one prow, on the right (SSW). In reality the ribbon sits in a flat-faced channel between two separate blades. The NE blade is narrow and sharp-edged and rises to a pointed tip well above the flare rim, near cab-sill height. The SW blade is a broad wing with a horizontally louvred face, a flat top sloping up outward and a rounded outer edge. Both blades have full-height creases that diverge upward. The ribbon's top edge is slanted, and the ribbon shows a 2-column mullion grid with about 25 rows. BT-01 shows only concentric circles, with no notch or blades in plan. This is the tower's signature from the AirTrain and the roadways; anyone who knows SFO would see the drawn tower as a generic round 'torch'.
findings.evidence: refs/cache/buildings/review_likeness/t4.jpg (Famartin, CC BY-SA 4.0, bearing 338; crop at display (640-1560, 200-900)): NE blade tip at about display (800,245), against the round flare rim at about y 310 on that side, so about 65 px or 2.4 m above it at 0.037 m/px from the 387-px cab roof. Ribbon top runs from display y 205 (NE side) to 265 (SW side). The SW wing face has horizontal louvre striations and a rounded outer edge at x about 1005 in the crop. t3.jpg (bearing 319): same blades. A luminance profile down the ribbon gives a row pitch of about 33 px, i.e. about 25 rows over 830 px, which matches spec ribbon_width.note. Two columns are visible from bottom to top. The spec still records 'fin / blade plan geometry NOT known [unk]'.
findings.fix: Draw both blades and the recessed ribbon channel in BT-02 B (NE tip above the rim, SW louvred wing) and the notch in the BT-01 plan, tagged obs-photo / inf, with the slanted ribbon head and the mullion grid.

findings.where: docs/drawings/buildings/BI-02 view 1 (west elevation)
findings.problem: The west facade fill runs from roof tip to roof tip across the full 252.9 m, up to the glazed tip bands. In reality the end walls are set back about 20 m from the tips, and the gull-wing roof cantilevers open beyond them, with sky and soffit visible under each tip. This open overhang is the ITB's defining silhouette. The sheet contradicts its own BI-03, which draws the 705-ft (214.9 m) hall floor inside the 252.9 m roof (about 19 m per side).
findings.evidence: refs/cache/buildings/review_likeness/i4.jpg (DimiCalifornia, public domain, near-frontal long lens; zoom of x 60-1060 px). Left roof tip is at about x 73 and the end-wall corner at about x 230: 157 px. The scale from the crown, at x about 1020, to the left tip gives 947 px = 126.4 m, so 0.1335 m/px and about 21 m of open cantilever. i1.jpg (panorama) shows the same open tips. The draw_itb.py comments and BI-02 view 2 note the end-wall set-back as text only.
findings.fix: In view 1, stop the wall fill at the end walls (705 ft hall, set-back inf) and leave the wing tips as open cantilevers with the soffit line.

findings.where: BI-02 view 1 and BI-03 view 2 (cross-section at u = +57.9)
findings.problem: The roof is drawn as a single eave line over a facade fill that reaches up to it. The columns are thin construction lines. Photos show a different arrangement. The west facade's glass wall is flat-topped, at about 9 m below the eave crest on the wings. Above it, the deep triangulated 'football' truss of the outer truss line is exposed along the whole facade and tapers toward the tips. The big white columns stand in front of the glass on the departures curb and branch into diagonal struts into the truss. BI-03's cross-section instead places the 'west glass wall (3 layers of frit) position = eave line [inf]' at the roof edge, with the outer truss line 8.4 m inside it. The photos put the wall behind the outer column line.
findings.evidence: i4.jpg: wing glass-wall top is level at y about 380 px; roof crest at y about 310. That is about 70 px, or 9.3 m, of exposed truss band, which compares with the published 29-ft (8.8 m) truss depth. Each white column casts its shadow onto the fritted wall, so it stands clear of the wall. i3.jpg (Elizabeth K. Joseph, CC BY 2.0): the column at x about 360-430 rises from the curb sidewalk in front of the glazed entrance level, with V-struts into the truss at y about 150-300. The roof soffit and trusses overhang the curb.
findings.fix: Draw the exposed truss band (inf profile from depth()) in the elevation above a level glass-wall head. Draw the columns as solid members outside the wall plane with their branching struts. Move the BI-03 west wall behind the outer truss line, tagged obs-photo.

findings.where: BI-02 view 1 and BI-03 view 1 (solid eave line), draw_itb.py eave() and crown()
findings.problem: The solid (primary) roof silhouette is flat at the notch height of about 35.7 m across the central section: eave() clamps |u| < 23 to the value at 23 m. The glazed centre crown appears only as a dashed curve. In photos the centre section is a full convex arch with a glazed lens crown as high as, or slightly higher than, the wing humps. It meets the wings at sharp V notches. A reader of the solid line sees a flat-topped saddle in the middle of the ITB, which is not there.
findings.evidence: i4.jpg: left wing crest at y about 312 px, centre glazed crown at y about 303, right crest at about 305. The notches are sharp cusps at x about 800 and about 1225 (y about 345). Between them the roof is one continuous arch about 425 px (about 57 m) wide. i1.jpg shows the same three-hump silhouette. The spec itself has crown 40.1 m [obs, photo ±2].
findings.fix: Draw the centre arch as the primary silhouette, in the obs style with its ±2 m band, and keep the flat 35.7 m only at the notch points.

findings.where: BD-01 (BA-D head) and BD-02 view 1b; draw_domestic.py
findings.problem: The BA-D head is drawn as the bare SFO Museum outline and, in section, as a flat 118.7 m × 8.49 m box. The research records 'a large trapezoidal head with two semicircular features and linear skylights', and T2's published roof is 'floating angular planes'. The head's rotunda drums and angular low roof planes, which identify BA-D from the air and the apron, are missing from both plan and section.
findings.evidence: out/buildings/drawings/BD-01_naip.jpg: a full circular roof element at the NW part of the head and a semicircular drum on its S edge. refs/cache/buildings/review_likeness/a1.jpg (Pi.1415926535, CC BY-SA 4.0/GFDL, Sep 2025, from the NE; crop x 0-1060, y 540-830): a low round drum with a flat roof at the head and dark angular roof planes beside it. docs/research/buildings_domestic.md §4, BA-D. There is no rotunda or semicircle code in draw_domestic.py.
findings.fix: Add the two drums (plan from NAIP, height unk) and the skylight lines to BD-01, and show the drum in the BD-02 1b section.

findings.where: BD-01 (BA-F), BD-02 view 1
findings.problem: The BA-F hub is drawn as the merged outline where the NW and NE arms meet. The research records 'an octagonal rotunda hub with arms [pub, CDR massing; obs]', and NAIP shows an octagonal roof with a concentric octagonal lantern or skylight ring. The NW arm's long central roof monitor (a light strip along its centreline) is also not drawn. BD-02 has no section of the hub or of the NW arm. Of the T3 piers, only the NE arm is shown.
findings.evidence: out/buildings/drawings/BD-01_naip.jpg, crop of sheet area (280-620, 110-380) at 1800 px width: the octagon with an inner octagon at the arm junction, and a continuous central light strip along the NW arm. docs/research/buildings_domestic.md §5.4.
findings.fix: Draw the octagonal hub and lantern and the NW-arm monitor from NAIP (obs plan, heights unk), and add a hub section.

findings.where: BD-01 (BA-B), BD-02 view 1 (BA-B south half)
findings.problem: The BA-B raised central clerestory (19.0 m) is hatched only over about 60 m at the south tip. The rest of the 400-m pier reads as one flat 13.1 m roof. NAIP shows the PV-covered central band running continuously from the T1 Center junction to the tip. The published design is a pier with a central clerestory along the concourse. The likeness of BA-B is its long raised spine, not a tip-only bump.
findings.evidence: out/buildings/drawings/BD-01_naip.jpg, crop at sheet (380-920, 560-1150): the PV rows on the central band are continuous along the pier. BD-01 label: 'raised part ~33 m wide (hatched, approx.)' at t -1238..-1176 only. The research admits 'BA-B north half not measured'.
findings.fix: Draw the central band along the whole pier from NAIP, tagged inf where the height is not measured, rather than leaving it flat.

findings.where: BL-03 view 4 (Superbay, across the spine); draw_landside.py sheet_elev V4
findings.problem: The flanking cantilever bays are drawn as flat-topped boxes at 120 ft (36.6 m) either side of a 135-ft spine block, a stepped 'castle' silhouette. 120 ft is the published interior height. The research's own deviation table says 'cantilevered roofs falling to the doors'. The reference photo shows roof planes falling from the central ridge to an eave over the door line well below the ridge, a folded sawtooth eave (the 8 × 17.3 m bays) and faceted hipped ends.
findings.evidence: refs/cache/buildings/review_likeness/l3.jpg (BrokenSphere, CC BY-SA 3.0; identification as the Superbay is the spec's own and unverified). Door and wall face from the eave at y about 515-530 px to the base at about 690 (about 175 px). The roof rises a further about 90 px to the ridge at y about 425. If the ridge is 41.1 m, the eave is roughly 27 m. The sawtooth eave is on the right half and the triangular facets on the left. docs/research/buildings_landside.md, model table: 'Superbay … cantilevered roofs falling to the doors'.
findings.fix: Draw sloping cantilever roofs from the spine to an inf/unk eave height, with the folded eave, rather than flat 120-ft boxes.

findings.where: BL-03 view 2 (Grand Hyatt)
findings.problem: The hotel is drawn as one 107 m × 44 m box with 12 equal floors from grade. The spec photo notes and the research describe a crescent slab with a concave east face, a podium (lobby and AirTrain at the 4th floor), a taller or narrower north block, a rooftop penthouse and corner masts. A viewer would not recognise the drawn box.
findings.evidence: refs/cache/buildings/review_likeness/l4.jpg (Gregory Varnum, CC BY-SA 4.0): a dark metal-panel podium about 3 floors high (y 895-1065 px) under the left part of the face. About 9.4 glass floors sit above it at about 55 px per floor. A dark penthouse about 1.4 floors high sits right of centre (x 990-1395, y 310-385). There is a separate end block at the left edge and obstruction-light masts at the corners. docs/research/buildings_landside.md model table: 'crescent tower plus podium, not one block'.
findings.fix: Draw the podium, the slab, the penthouse and the end block as separate masses, with heights tagged inf.

findings.where: BI-01 views 3 and 4 (Boarding Areas A and G); draw_itb.py lines 170-172
findings.problem: The raised roof pods are given only as labels ('3 raised D-shaped pods 70/55/55 m', '3 raised lens pods 60/55/62 m'). They are not drawn in plan or in any elevation, although BA-A pod 1 is a DOF point 8 m above the main roof. They are the main roof features of both boarding areas.
findings.evidence: out/buildings/drawings/BI-01_naip.jpg, BA-G panel: three raised elliptical volumes clearly imaged on the roof. refs/cache/buildings/review_likeness/a2.jpg (Pi.1415926535, CC BY-SA 4.0, Sep 2025): raised oval drums with rounded ends, about one storey above the BA-G roof (x 40-510 and 1100-1560 px, y 780-900). A grep for 'pod' in draw_itb.py finds only leaders and the DOF marker.

findings.where: BT-02 views A and B (upper slots)
findings.problem: The 49.2-56.8 m slot band is drawn as uniform hatching across the full width, and in view B also across the landside blades. Photos show discrete narrow dark slots, about 1 m wide, all leaning the same way: about 7 visible across the airside half, so about 12-14 round the round body. On the landside they appear only on the round body NE of the ribbon, none on the SW louvred wing. Some slots have a glazed window in their lower end. The flare's widest line is drawn as a sharp corner with a short vertical lip; photos show a rounded shoulder curving in to the cab deck.
findings.evidence: t2.jpg (Famartin, airside, bearing 126): 6-7 slots between display y about 510 and 720, the bottoms cut on a ring seam. t1.jpg crop (800-1250, 100-450): 7 parallelogram slots. t4.jpg crop: 3 slots left of the ribbon, the lower one glazed at display (310-345, 510-630) in the crop. None on the right wing. Band heights agree with the spec: t1 gives 49.6-57.1 m on the rim and D anchor.
findings.fix: Draw individual slots (count and lean inf from photos) on the round body only, and round the flare shoulder.

findings.where: BT-02 view A (single lower slot); draw_tower.py, poly (0.6,a)-(1.6,a)-(3.4,b)-(2.4,b)
findings.problem: The lower airside slot is drawn with a 1.8 m sideways shift over its 17 m height, about 6° from vertical. Two photos from different bearings both show it leaning about 15-16°, with its top close to the right silhouette.
findings.evidence: t2.jpg: dark-pixel centre of the slot moves from display x about 780 at y 940 to x about 746 at y 1060, i.e. 34 px per 120 px, about 16°. t1.jpg: about (1075,525) to (1010,760), 65/235 px, about 15.5°. Slot top is about 5 m right of the axis at 0.0698 m/px. Width (about 1 m) and length (about 16.7 m) agree with the drawing.
findings.fix: Re-measure the slot's top and bottom offsets and redraw it at about 15°, tagged inf-photo.

findings.where: BT-02 (masts), draw_tower.py 'masts (count changes over time; 2-3 shown)'
findings.problem: Four masts are drawn. The spec's own note gives 'about 8 masts' in 2015 and 'about 12 masts + camera poles' in 2025, spread round the whole rim at several heights. The 2015 photo also shows a lattice instrument boom (a mast with a cross-arm) standing on the flare deck beside the cab. It is not drawn.
findings.evidence: t1.jpg crop (800-1250, 100-450): 8 masts, plus the boom at crop (140-275, 185-310). t3.jpg / t4.jpg (2025): 12-14 masts plus cameras. spec_tower.json h_antenna_tips.note.
findings.fix: Draw the 2025 mast set (positions inf from the photos) and the flare-deck boom, if still present.

findings.where: BT-02 views A and B (base building), BT-01
findings.evidence: t1.jpg crop (700-1300, 600-950): two dark textured rooftop boxes flanking the shaft with thin white canopy plates. t2.jpg: a tall dark louvred block right of the shaft (display x 915-1060, y 1430-1560) and a dark ribbon window band at y about 1600-1700. t4.jpg: a curtain-wall bay below the ribbon (display x 900-1355, y 1680-2000).
findings.fix: Add these as obs-photo massing (heights inf) on BT-02, and mark their plan positions on BT-01 as approximate.

findings.where: BI-02 view 1 (facade), docs/drawings/buildings/README.md ('Facade mullion module unknown')
findings.evidence: i4.jpg zoom: canopy struts at crop x about 320, 450, 580, 715, 850 (×1/1.5 → about 88 px). That is about 11.8 m at 0.1335 m/px, consistent with the published 40-ft (12.19 m) truss grid. The wings' fritted walls are horizontally banded, and the centre bay is clear glass with the lettering (i1.jpg, i4.jpg).
findings.fix: Record the 40-ft module as obs-photo, and draw the canopy line, the strut rhythm and the wing / centre glazing split.

findings.where: BL-03 views 1-2 (Garages A and G), BL-02
findings.problem: Each garage is drawn as a 25 m box with a light-blue 25-41.5 m 'deck range' band over its full 282 m length. The sheet therefore reads as a 41.5 m-tall block. In reality the 37.6 / 39.6 m 'drum tops' are discrete round precast helix towers at the west ends, with perforated-metal screens, rising above a lower deck. The AirTrain guideway runs into each garage at Level 7, which is in the text only.
findings.evidence: refs/cache/buildings/review_likeness/l1.jpg (Pi.1415926535, CC BY-SA 4.0): the curved helix drum beside the guideway entering the Garage A station box. a2.jpg: Garage G's rounded west end with its rooftop drum. BL-02_naip.jpg: round helix structure at the west end of each outline.
findings.fix: Show the helix drum as its own round mass at the end, the deck range as a range bar (not a full-length band), and the guideway entry at L7.

findings.where: BL-03 view 3 (Rental Car Center)
findings.evidence: refs/cache/buildings/review_likeness/l5.jpg (Pi.1415926535, CC BY-SA 4.0): the canted corrugated band on the left, and the round perforated tower (display x 950-1305, y 185-990). spec_landside photo note lists both.
findings.fix: Draw the canted upper band and the cylindrical tower (heights inf / DOF 60 ft).

findings.where: BD-02 view 1 (BA-E), BD set as a whole
findings.problem:
1. BA-E is a plain rectangle. Its published roof is 'tapered edges overhanging clerestory glazing', and a1 shows a PV-covered roof with a clerestory band under an overhanging edge and a full-height glazed head end.
2. More broadly, the domestic set has no elevation of any landside hall: not the T1 Harvey Milk front, not T2, not T3. These are the faces travellers see from the AirTrain and the roadways. The T1 front is a two-tier fritted-glass wall with large lettering, a glass curb canopy and a PV roof. T3E has a large perforated-metal rooftop penthouse (CDR).
findings.evidence: a1.jpg crop (1040-1920, 560-880): BA-E roof with PV, a dark clerestory band below the roof edge, and a glazed head end. refs/cache/buildings/review_likeness/d1.jpg (Famartin, CC BY-SA 4.0): T1 landside facade. docs/research/buildings_domestic.md §5.2-5.3.
findings.fix: Show the BA-E fascia overhang and clerestory band in section, and add at least schematic landside elevations of T1, T2 and T3, with unknown heights drawn as unk placeholders.
